shortDescription: Australia's Ingenia Communities Group ASX:INA said on Monday it was assessing an improved A$2.14 billion ($1.50 billion) buyout offer from private equity firm Warburg Pincus after rejecting two earlier bids .Here are some more details:($1 = 1.4261 Australian dollars)

children: said on Monday it was assessing an improved A$2.14 billion ($1.50 billion) buyout offer from private equity firm Warburg Pincus after rejecting two earlier bids .
The latest offer, at A$5.25 per share, is nearly 4% higher than the previous bid of A$5.05 apiece, or A$2.06 billion, and represents a 16.7% premium to the stock's last close.
It is 10.5% higher than the initial approach of A$4.75 per share, or A$1.94 billion.
Ingenia had rejected the previous two proposals, saying they "substantially" undervalued the firm.
In the current offer, Warburg Pincus retained the earlier condition that Ingenia abandon its planned $711-million acquisition of master-planned communities developer Peet
, a deal Ingenia sees as central to its strategy.
Ingenia said its board was assessing the revised proposal and had not yet formed a view on the offer or its conditions.
The board did not make any recommendation to shareholders with respect to the offer.
